text:
Rina: spotted a weird p99 blip for /v2/generate (eu-west) ~21:40. p50/p95 steady but sample_count dropped ~4x for that slice.
Tom: same here. traffic shifted to lowmem-fallback pool around 21:36. that pool is downsampling telemetry.
Iris: is the dashboard using tdigest rollups or raw-event percentiles? need to know if this is a sketch artifact.
Rina: dashboard query uses tdigest_percentile(rollup_tdigest, 0.99) + sum(sample_count) from endpoint_latency_rollups (5m buckets).
Nate: downsampled source + tdigest merge = tail instability. options: show provenance/confidence in UI, or run an on-demand raw p99 job for that timeslice.
Tom: minimal approach: surface a small "trust" pill next to percentiles showing source (raw|downsampled) and sample_count, mark amber if samples < 200. add a "compute raw p99" CTA.
Iris: UX note: include estimated cost/time in the CTA (e.g., est $0.10, ~12s) and rate-limit per-org. otherwise ops will get spammed.
Rina: I'll run a micro-canary flipping telemetry.downsample=false for lowmem-fallback at 10% traffic for 15m to verify.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: config change requested by Rina - route lowmem-fallback telemetry.downsample=false (canary 10%).
Tom: also found inconsistent tags: some producers send route_id, others route_name. UI grouping breaks. we should normalize at ingestion or map aliases in the dashboard for now.
Nate: backend work: add POST /internal/metrics/raw_p99 to kick off the job and return job_id. UI polls job status.
Iris: I'll mock the trust pill: green=raw+>500 samples, amber=<500, red=unknown/no-origin. tooltip explains tdigest caveats and links to docs.
Rina: results from canary in ~20m. will attach before/after charts and tenant list.
Tom: if canary reverts p99 to baseline, we add the pill + docs and deprioritize changing routing.
Nate: also open a small RFC to standardize telemetry fields across producers. that'll avoid a bunch of UI heuristics.
Iris: good plan. I'll post mockups and the CTA flow for review when charts land.
Rina: thanks all, pinging back when data is in.
